topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by framing cancer evolution within the course context and outlining the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Cell-intrinsic genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how cell-intrinsic alterations confer selective growth advantages to evolving clones during early tumor progression.

topics.label: Tissue hierarchy and the cell of origin in cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how normal tissue differentiation hierarchies and stemness determine which cell types can initiate and propagate tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory support of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how external microenvironmental cues and non-cancerous supporting cells are required to enable both tumor initiation and established growth.

topics.label: Technologies for investigating tumor evolution and microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the experimental and computational tools used to map clonal evolution and cellular interactions within tumors.

topics.label: Multifactorial evolutionary model of cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides a comprehensive synthesis integrating diverse biological mechanisms into an overarching evolutionary framework of cancer development.

topics.label: Conclusion and preview of the next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and indicates the topic of the upcoming lecture.
